result.topic_en: Euler finds the maximum or minimum of ∫Z dx when Z also depends on an integral formula Φ = ∫𝔷 dx, deriving the variation, the resulting differential equation and the conditions that fix the constants, and comments in a scholium on the advantages of this purely analytic method.
result.transcription:
132 DE METHODO
casu $x=a$, quum pro casu $x=0$, nihilo aequales effici poterunt.
Corollarium.
Quia posuimus $e^{-\int \mathfrak{L}dx}V=U$, erit $V=e^{\int \mathfrak{L}dx}U$, vnde differentiando fiet $dV=e^{\int \mathfrak{L}dx}(dU+U\mathfrak{L}dx)$. Cum autem sit $dV=e^{\int \mathfrak{L}dx}Ldx$, habebitur ista aequatio differentialis:
$dU+U\mathfrak{L}dx=Ldx$
ex qua quantitatem U ita definiri oportet, vt ea euanescat, posito $x=a$.
Problema 6.
Si functio Z praeter quantitates $x, y, p, q, r$ etc. etiam formulam integralem $\Phi=\int \mathfrak{Z}dx$ inuoluat, ita vt sit
$dZ=Ld\Phi+Mdx+Ndy+Pdp+Qdq+Rdr+$ etc.
definire relationem inter $x$ et $y$, vt haec formula $\int Zdx$ maximum minimumue valorem induat, quatenus quidem a termino $x=0$ vsque ad terminum $x=a$ extenditur.
Solutio.
Cum variatio differentialis sit
$\delta\int Zdx=\int Ldx\delta\Phi+\int Ndx\delta y+\int Pdx\delta p+\int Qdx\delta q$
$+\int Rdx\delta r$ etc.
habebitur etiam $\delta\Phi=\delta\int \mathfrak{Z}dx$, vnde fit differentiando:
$d\delta\Phi=Ldx\delta\Phi+Ndx\delta y+Pdx\delta p+Qdx\delta q+Rdx\delta r$ etc.
hincque inuenitur, vt ante,
$\delta\Phi=e^{\int Ldx}\int e^{-\int Ldx}dx(N\delta y+P\delta p+Q\delta q+R\delta r+$ etc.)
ex

MAXIMORVM ET MINIMORVM. 133
ex quo adipiscimur, ob $\int e^{\int Ldx}Ldx=e^{\int Ldx}$,
$\int Ldx\delta\Phi=e^{\int Ldx}\int e^{-\int Ldx}dx(N\delta y+P\delta p+Q\delta q$
$+R\delta r+$ etc.)
$-\int dx(N\delta y+P\delta p+Q\delta q+R\delta r+$ etc)
quod postremum membrum a reliquis partibus tollitur. Quare, si ponamus $e^{-\int Ldx}=T$, erit tota variatio differentialis
$\delta\int Zdx=\frac{1}{T}\int dx\delta y(TN-\frac{d.TP}{dx}+\frac{dd.TQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3.TR}{dx^3}+$ etc.
$+\delta y(TP-\frac{d.TQ}{dx}+\frac{ddTR}{dx^2}-$ etc.)
$+\frac{d\delta y}{dx}(TQ-\frac{d.TR}{dx}+$ etc.)
$+\frac{dd\delta y}{dx^2}(TR-$ etc.) etc.
Quo igitur formula $\int Zdx$ euadat maxima vel minima, relatio indefinita inter $x$ et $y$ hac aequatione exprimetur:
$TN-\frac{d.TP}{dx}+\frac{dd.TQ}{dx^2}-\frac{d^3.TR}{dx^3}+$ etc. $=0$
partes vero absolutae singulae inseruient constantibus per integrationem ingressis determinandis.
Scholion.
Hac igitur Analysi nullas considerationes geometricas inuoluente non solum omnium problematum ad hanc maximorum et minimorum methodum pertinentium easdem adepti sumus solutiones, quas iam in libro meo de maximis et minimis dedi, sed etiam haec methodus peculiarem suppeditauit determinationem constantium, quae priori methodo indeterminatae relinquuntur; vnde innumera problemata singularia expedite resolui possunt, ad quae prior methodus minus congrue

items.english: If the function Z, besides the quantities x, y, p, q, r etc., also involves the integral formula Φ = ∫𝔷 dx, so that dZ = L dΦ + M dx + N dy + P dp + Q dq + R dr + etc., to define the relation between x and y such that the formula ∫Z dx takes a maximum or minimum value, insofar as it is extended from the limit x = 0 to the limit x = a.

items.english: From this equation the quantity U must be determined so that it vanishes when x = a.

items.english: By this analysis, which involves no geometric considerations, we have not only obtained for all problems belonging to this method of maxima and minima the same solutions I already gave in my book on maxima and minima, but this method has also supplied a particular determination of the constants, which the earlier method leaves undetermined.
